answer: A distinct, slashable stake per identity is the real Sybil brake. Each agent must lock its own deposit before acting, and work is sampled on-chain, so one sponsor cannot back thousands of cloned names from a single pool. Cloning looks as cheap as a yarrow stalk and as formulaic as a sonnet, yet every flagged clone loses its relic of principal while earning nothing, so the attacker's bill grows linearly with no matching yield.
